_meta.name: English
_meta.note: Every string a person reads in the window. A new language is a new file beside this one, never a change in code - ADR-21. The keys are English too, and they are what the code refers to.

gui.window.title: Better Windows Services
gui.column.name: Name
gui.action.stop.hint: Show what stopping the entries you picked would do. Nothing is changed until you carry it out.
gui.action.start.hint: Show what starting the entries you picked would do. Nothing is changed until you carry it out.
gui.action.restart.hint: Show what restarting the entries you picked would do. Nothing is changed until you carry it out.
gui.action.elevate.hint: Start this tool again with administrator rights. Windows will ask you to confirm. Your columns come back on their own, anything typed in the search box does not.
gui.action.startType.hint: Show what setting the start type of the entries you picked would do. Nothing is changed until you carry it out.
gui.action.refresh.hint: Read the machine again, in full, including the settings a listing does not watch. F5 does the same.
gui.action.export.hint: Write what the list shows to a comma separated file - the entries that are on screen, the columns you have on, in the order you sorted them.
gui.action.needsPick: Pick one or more entries in the list first.
gui.columns.hint: Choose what the list shows. Drag a heading to move a column and its edge to resize. What you choose is kept, so the list opens the way you left it.
gui.details.close.hint: Close the panel. Escape does the same, and clears the query when there is no panel.
gui.details.gone: This entry is no longer in the listing, so what is below is the last thing this window read about it.
gui.overview.title: This machine, before you ask it anything
gui.overview.hint: What this machine looks like right now. Every number is a question you can ask again - click one and it goes into the search box.
gui.overview.notUp: set to start automatically and did not come up
gui.overview.notUp.template: more are per-user templates, which never run because a session copy runs instead
gui.overview.notUp.trigger: more are waiting for a trigger, so they are stopped because nothing has asked for them
gui.overview.orphans: orphans - set to start automatically and the file is gone
gui.overview.fileGone: point at a file that is not there, whatever their start type
gui.overview.notYet: How many entries are not from a stock Windows is not counted yet. It needs the stock baseline, which arrives with the snapshot work - this screen will say so rather than show a number it cannot stand behind.
gui.overview.dismiss.hint: Put this away and show the list. Clicking any number above does the same, and takes its question with it.
gui.overview.button.hint: What this machine looks like right now - how much is running, what did not come up, and what points at a file that is gone.
gui.layout.ignored: The kept column layout names columns this window could not use, so they were left out: {0}
gui.layout.noneShown: The kept column layout hides every column, so the usual ones are shown instead.
gui.layout.widths: A kept width could not be read for these columns, so they start where the theme puts them: {0}
gui.layout.unreadable: The kept column layout could not be read, so the usual columns are shown. The file was moved to {1} rather than overwritten. {0}
gui.layout.unreadableStays: The kept column layout could not be read, so the usual columns are shown. It could not be moved out of the way, so this will happen again. {0}
gui.layout.otherSchema: The kept column layout was written against schema version {0} and this program reads version {1}, so it was left alone and the usual columns are shown.
gui.layout.carriedForward: The kept column layout was written against schema version {0} and has been carried forward to version {1}. Your columns are as you left them, and the file will be saved in the newer shape the next time you change one.
gui.layout.notKept: The column layout was not saved, so this window will open the way it did last time. {0}
gui.layout.noProfile: Windows names no application data folder for this account, so there is nowhere to keep the layout.
gui.search.tip.what: Type a word to search, or write a query: a field, a colon and a value. Put ! in front of a member to exclude it, and give a field twice to mean either.
gui.search.tip.regex: Between slashes it is a regular expression, so /^win.*svc$/ finds names that begin with win and end in svc.
gui.example.shouldBeRunning: Set to start and not running
gui.example.missingFile: The file it runs is not there
gui.filter.hint.adds: Each of these writes what it stands for into the box, so the filter you clicked is a query you can read and edit. Two of these show both.
gui.filter.hint.narrows: Each of these writes what it stands for into the box, so the filter you clicked is a query you can read and edit. Each one narrows the list on its own.
gui.filter.toggle.hint: Show or hide the filters. What is on stays on either way - each one writes into the search box, so a hidden filter is still there to read in the query.
gui.instances.toggle.hint: Windows makes a private copy of some services for every account that signs in - CDPUserSvc_1a2b3 beside CDPUserSvc - and lists them like any other service. This window folds each copy under the service it came from and counts them beside its name. Turn this on to give every copy a row of its own.
gui.scope.services.hint: Services only - what services.msc shows. Drivers are left out of this list, so a search here never reaches one.
gui.scope.drivers.hint: Drivers only - kernel and file system drivers, which services.msc does not show at all. They are listed here and cannot be started or stopped.
gui.scope.all.hint: Everything the service manager holds, services and drivers in one list. Use it to see a service beside the driver it needs.
gui.scope.hint: Which list this is. The search below asks inside it.
gui.status.failed: Could not read the service control manager. {0}
gui.status.partial.many: {0} entries were judged on a field that could not be read, so this list may be missing entries, or holding ones that do not belong.
gui.status.partial.one: {0} entry was judged on a field that could not be read, so this list may be missing an entry, or holding one that does not belong.
gui.status.tooCostly.many: The expression ran out of time on {0} entries, so they were never checked. Try a simpler one.
gui.status.tooCostly.one: The expression ran out of time on {0} entry, so it was never checked. Try a simpler one.
gui.status.folded.one: {0} per-user instance is folded under the template it came from. Show every instance lists it on its own.
gui.status.folded.many: {0} per-user instances are folded under the templates they came from. Show every instance lists them on their own.
gui.status.holding: The list is holding still while you use it, so nothing joins or leaves under your cursor. It settles when you move away, or on F5.
gui.status.notElevated: Running without administrator rights, so Windows hands over fewer entries than it has.
gui.plan.blocked.notElevated: Not running as administrator, so the service manager would refuse every step. Restart as admin to carry this out.
gui.plan.blocked.running: This plan is being carried out now. Interrupt stops it before the next step.
gui.plan.blocked.alreadyDone: This plan has already been carried out. Close the panel and pick the entries again to do anything else.
gui.plan.blocked.nothingToRun: Nothing here can be carried out. What is in the way is listed above.
gui.plan.notice.running: Carrying this out now. Interrupting stops the steps that have not started - steps that give something back still run.
gui.plan.notice.done.one: Done. The entry is where you asked.
gui.plan.notice.done.many: Done. All {0} entries are where you asked.
gui.plan.notice.partly.one: The entry is not where you asked. What did not is below.
gui.plan.notice.partly.many: {0} of {1} entries are where you asked. What did not is below.
gui.plan.extra.one: One entry comes along that nobody picked: {0}
gui.plan.extra.many: {0} entries come along that nobody picked: {1}
gui.plan.overlapping: Named more than once, because one pick is inside another's cascade: {0}. The second attempt finds it already where the first put it.
gui.plan.warning.cascade.one: Stopping {0} also stops one other entry: {2}
gui.plan.warning.inTheWay.one: This is running and needs {0}, and it is not included: {1}. The stop will be refused while it runs.
gui.plan.warning.inTheWay.many: These are running and need {0}, and they are not included: {1}. The stop will be refused while they run.
gui.plan.warning.sharedProcess.one: {0} shares its process with: {1}. That keeps running and the process does not go away.
gui.plan.warning.sharedProcess.many: {0} shares its process with: {1}. Those keep running and the process does not go away.
gui.plan.warning.returnsAfterReboot: {0} starts automatically, so it will be back after the next restart.
gui.plan.warning.cascadeUnreadable: Could not read what depends on {0}, so more may stop than this shows.
gui.plan.warning.alreadyThere: {0} is already in that state, so nothing would change.
gui.plan.problem.unknownService.one: There is no service called {0} any more.
gui.plan.problem.unknownService.many: {0} of these are not services any more: {1}
gui.plan.problem.notOperable.one: {0} is a driver. This tool shows drivers but does not start or stop them.
gui.plan.problem.notOperable.many: {0} of these are drivers. This tool shows drivers but does not start or stop them: {1}
gui.plan.problem.cascadeNotOperable.one: Getting to {0} would mean stopping this driver first: {1}. This tool does not stop drivers.
gui.plan.problem.cascadeNotOperable.many: Getting to {0} would mean stopping these drivers first: {1}. This tool does not stop drivers.
gui.plan.problem.cannotComeBack.one: Restarting {0} would take this down and could not start it again, because it is disabled: {1}
gui.plan.problem.cannotComeBack.many: Restarting {0} would take these down and could not start them again, because they are disabled: {1}
gui.plan.carryOut.hint: Do the steps above, in that order, on this machine.
gui.plan.interrupt.hint: Stop before the next step. Anything already taken down is still put back.
gui.plan.failure.timedOut: {0} did not finish the {1} while we watched. It may arrive by itself.
gui.plan.failure.refusedStartType: The start type of {0} could not be changed: {1}
gui.plan.close.hint: Close this. Escape does the same.
gui.start.mark.missing: The file this entry is set to launch is not on disk.
gui.start.mark.disabled: Disabled. It will not start, by itself or on request.
gui.start.mark.unknown: The start type could not be read on this account.
gui.start.mark.boot: Started by the boot loader, before the system does anything else.
gui.start.mark.system: Started by the kernel during system initialisation.
gui.start.mark.automatic: Started by the manager when the system starts.
gui.start.mark.manual: Started only when something asks for it.
gui.against.mark.yes: Set to start automatically and it is not running, and nothing is waiting to start it either.
gui.against.mark.unknown: Whether it matches its start type could not be worked out, because the start type could not be read.
gui.elevate.refused: The tool was not started again as administrator, so nothing has changed and this window is the one you had.
gui.elevate.failed: The tool could not be started again as administrator. {0}
gui.elevate.noPath: Windows does not say where this program is on disk, so it cannot be started again.
gui.export.failed: The list could not be written. {0}
gui.export.name: services
gui.empty.nothingMatched: Nothing on this machine matches what you asked for.
gui.empty.nothingMatchedWayOut: Press Esc to empty the box.
gui.empty.nothingMatchedHere: Nothing in this list matches what you asked for.
gui.empty.nothingMatchedHereWayOut: Press Esc to empty the box, or choose All above to search the whole machine.
gui.empty.askedForDrivers: You asked for drivers, and this is the list of services.
gui.empty.askedForServices: You asked for services, and this is the list of drivers.
gui.empty.askedElsewhereWayOut: Choose that list above, or press Esc to empty the box.
gui.empty.nothingToShow: The service control manager handed over no entries at all.
gui.empty.failed: The list could not be read. What went wrong is written under it.
gui.empty.failedWayOut: Press F5 to read the machine again.
gui.query.unreadSignatures: This asks about signatures, which are not read for a listing, so no entry can answer it here. Ask the command line with --signatures.
gui.query.readingSignatures: This asks about signatures, which are being read now. The answer is incomplete until they arrive.
gui.query.readingMemory: This asks about memory, which is being read now. The answer is incomplete until it arrives.
gui.query.unreadMemory: This asks about memory, which is not read for a listing, so no entry can answer it here. Ask the command line with --memory.
gui.query.unknownField: There is no field called {0}. Fields you can use: {1}.
gui.query.unknownValueNearest: {1} has no value {0}. Did you mean {2}? It accepts: {3}.
gui.query.badPattern: The expression /{0}/ could not be read. {1}
gui.query.unclosedQuote: A quote is opened and never closed, starting at: {0}
gui.query.badNumber: {1} expects a number like 1234, >1000, <500, >=100 or 100-200. It got: {0}
gui.query.emptyTerm: {0} says nothing. A ! needs something after it, and a word needs something in it.
gui.query.patternTooComplex: The wildcard starting {0} has too many parts to build. Use fewer * and ? characters.
gui.query.badSize: {1} expects a size with a unit, like 500MB, >1GB, <100MB or 100MB-1GB. It got: {0}
